result.summary: Type E design artefact validated against all 9 acceptance criteria. (1) lint_design_artefact.py exits 0 with no findings. (2) Type E classification correct per lego-catalog.md §Selection rules: registry-channel migration, fail/runtime discriminator on ScriptResult, conditional payload assembly, and cross-module orchestration across executor/host_api/events/service_catalog/host_context — none map to Type A (CRUD endpoint), Type B (list page), Type C (DB migration), or Type D (React Flow node). (3) All MUST acceptance criteria covered: LUA-12 (real HTTP call path, single-table return shape, catalog lookup defense-in-depth), LUA-15 (LUA_REGISTRYINDEX migration, ScriptResult.error_kind discriminator, buildScriptFailedPayload constructor), LUA-16 (lua_getstack/lua_getinfo walk, conditional ScriptErrorPayload construction, capabilities_at_failure skip-reason). (4) No implementation code violating Type E rules: 8 zig blocks contain type signatures (struct/enum/pub fn/p pub extern fn); 4 blocks include illustrative deinit method bodies consistent with repo precedent (iss0173-gh501-jwks-zig016-fix.md establishes this convention) documenting the field-ownership contract that BACKEND-DEV must replicate. No business-logic implementation, no HTTP client wiring, no executeSource branch bodies, no captureStackTrace bodies. (5) Public function signatures complete: ScriptResult.deinit, ExecutionContext.service_catalog/instruction_limiter, host_context.setExplicitFailure/readExplicitFailure/clearExplicitFailure, events.buildScriptFailedPayload/buildScriptErrorPayload, luajit_bindings extern declarations. (6) Error taxonomy (per-design §4) enumerates 11 error sources across host_api/fail.zig, host_api/call_service.zig, executor.zig, luajit_bindings.zig, mapped to ScriptResult.error_kind values. (7) Dependencies (per-design §6.1) and out-of-scope items (per-design §6.2) explicit, including the CTX-1 service_catalog lifetime invariant, the engine-side worker boundary, and the explicit exclusion of LUA-11/13/08/09 from this branch. (8) Sequencing LUA-15 -> LUA-12 -> LUA-16 justified per per-design §7: LUA-15 first establishes the ScriptResult.error_kind discriminator and the registry channel that LUA-16 reuses in the same failed-pcall branch; LUA-12 is independent and can be inserted between them, but lands second because ExecutionContext field layout is stable after LUA-15; LUA-16 lands last because it touches the most files and depends conditionally on LUA-08/09. (9) Test plan covers exactly 26 cases (TC-LUA-12-impl-01..10 = 10, TC-LUA-15-impl-01..08 = 8, TC-LUA-16-impl-01..08 = 8; verified mechanically, no gaps, no duplicates). (10) Decisions D-1..D-4 traceable: D-1 to diagnosis F-LUA-12-2 (ServiceCatalog zero callers) and lua-integration.md §17.1; D-2 to diagnosis F-LUA-12-3 (return-shape divergence) and lua-integration.md §17.1; D-3 to diagnosis F-LUA-16-3 (instruction_count no source) and the LUA-08 deferred status in requirements.yaml; D-4 to diagnosis F-LUA-16-1 (captureStackTrace not implemented) and vendor/luajit/src/ldebug.h (function names verified).

issues.description: The design artefact includes 4 deinit method bodies (§2.1 ScriptResult.deinit, §2.4 ScriptErrorPayload.deinit, §10.1 same body duplicated as BACKEND-DEV implementation note, §10.2 EventRecord.deinit quoted from existing events.zig:54-57). These are illustrative contracts documenting the field-ownership pattern; they are consistent with the established repo precedent (iss0173-gh501-jwks-zig016-fix.md, 1 such block; validator PASS). Strict reading of 'no implementation code' would flag them as out of scope for Type E. Left as-is because (a) the bodies communicate the deinit contract that BACKEND-DEV must replicate across new fields, and (b) removing them would force BACKEND-DEV to infer the same pattern from prose alone. If a stricter reading is enforced in future, these bodies should move into the implementation-note sections and the type-definition sections should keep only field signatures.

OQ-3 documents that the production HTTP client (the function pointer the real-call path invokes) is NOT introduced in this design. Tests use a Zig function pointer stub per T-1. If the engine-side worker has no existing hook to inject the real HTTP client into ExecutionContext, this becomes a follow-up ISS. CODE-DESIGNER already raised this as MAJOR in their result.issues[0] (OPEN-LUA-12-HTTP-CLIENT-PROD). Confirmed: the design does NOT add an http_client_fn field to ExecutionContext (§2.2) and the production wiring is explicitly out of scope (§10.3). BACKEND-DEV must flag this during implementation if no hook exists.

D-2 (single response table for LUA-12) is a breaking change for scripts using `local body, status = platform.call_service(...)`. CHANGELOG draft text is included in §10.4, but DOC-UPDATER (Step 7) must add it alongside the requirement-status update. Confirmed dependency: implementation in BACKEND-DEV can land without CHANGELOG being merged; DOC-UPDATER adds it.
